narrativeProgression.description: Bakich begins by stating the 2024 eclipse will have a longer duration of totality than normal.
He provides the average duration of totality for most eclipses (3 minutes 40 seconds).
He highlights that the 2024 eclipse will last 4 minutes or longer along the centerline.
Bakich explains that the centerline stretches from the Mexico border to Indianapolis.
He compares the 2024 eclipse to the 2017 eclipse, noting that more people live in the path of totality this time.
Bakich emphasizes that 31.5 million people live within the path of totality for the 2024 eclipse.
He concludes by encouraging everyone in the path to step outside and enjoy the eclipse.
